newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dehaene wants to meet Jospin over Renault soon.
newsitem.headline: Dehaene wants to meet Jospin over Renault soon.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday he wanted to discuss the controversial closure of the Belgian Renault plant with his French socialist counterpart Lionel Jospin before June 10.
On that day there are meetings of the Renault board and of the French carmaker's shareholders.
Dehaene, who has branded the closure "unacceptable", told parliament that if he could not go to Paris, he would contact Jospin by telephone.
Jospin said last week, before Sunday's parliamentary elections which he won, that he would ask Renault to study alternatives to allow the assembly plant in Vilvoorde to remain open.
Renault, which announced the closure with 3,100 job losses in February, reiterated on Wednesday that it was indispensable to cut costs and streamline its European car assembly operations.
The French Socialist Party said on Wednesday it opposed the closure

"The Socialist Party...asks the management to halt the procedure to close the plant, to reopen the case and take up negotiations," a representative said after a meeting with a Vilvoorde workers' delegation at the party's headquarters.
Renault lost 5.25 billion francs ($901.2 million) last year and is struggling to break even this year.
